title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Funding Fee Financing, Remittance Period and Late Charge
content:
Under the VA Home Loan Guaranty, each program states whether the funding fee may be added to the loan amount, the number of calendar days after closing within which the lender must remit the funding fee to VA, and the late charge on a funding fee remitted after that deadline, as a percent of the fee.

## Terms by program

| Program | Fee may be financed into the loan | Remittance period (calendar days after closing) | Late charge on late remittance (% of the fee) |
|---|---|---|---|
| VA Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) | Yes | 15 | 4.0 |
| VA Manufactured Home Loan | Yes | 15 | 4.0 |
| VA Purchase Loan (10% or More Down) | Yes | 15 | 4.0 |
| VA Purchase Loan (5% to Less Than 10% Down) | Yes | 15 | 4.0 |
| VA Purchase Loan (Less Than 5% Down) | Yes | 15 | 4.0 |
| VA Cash-Out Refinance Loan | Yes | 15 | 4.0 |
| Native American Direct Loan (NADL) | Yes | 15 | 4.0 |

## Points of reading

- The remittance period runs in calendar days from the closing date; the obligation to remit rests on the lender.
- The late charge is a percentage of the fee itself and attaches only to a fee remitted after the remittance deadline.
- The terms are the same on all seven programs.

## Hypothetical illustration

A lender holding a hypothetical funding fee of 2,000.00 dollars that remits it after the 15-day period adds a late charge of 4.0 percent of the fee, that is 2,000.00 multiplied by 4.0 and divided by one hundred, or 80.00 dollars. The same fee remitted within the 15 days carries no late charge.
